answer: We establish Sybil resistance via dynamic opportunity-cost bonds, subgame-perfect slashing matrices, and zero-knowledge verifiable delay to define strict cryptoeconomic primitives. Enforcing staking collateral and slashing penalties proves that an adversary expanding across an isolated island into a dense nebula at dawn yields a strictly negative expected payoff for identity multiplication. Thus, this capital barrier guarantees negative expected attack utility, driving the system deterministically toward a robust Nash equilibrium within adversarial environments.
